q: Which ovarian cell type gives rise to most malignant ovarian tumors?
x: Surface epithelium, the lining of the ovary and fallopian tube, gives rise to about 90 percent of malignant ovarian tumors. Most are high-grade serous carcinomas in older women.

w.Germ cells: Germ cell tumors are the common ovarian neoplasms of girls and young women, but most are benign dermoids and make up a small share of cancers.
w.Granulosa cells: Granulosa cell tumors are uncommon estrogen-making sex cord-stromal tumors with Call-Exner bodies and inhibin as the marker.
w.Theca cells: Theca cells give rise to thecomas, which are benign, estrogen-making stromal tumors and rare compared with epithelial cancers.
w.Stromal fibroblasts: Stromal fibroblasts give rise to fibromas, benign solid tumors that can cause Meigs syndrome. They are never the main source of cancers.

pt.say: The surface epithelium column comes first because it gives rise to most ovarian cancers, mainly in older women with a raised CA-125.

q: Which marker rises with an ovarian tumor that shows Schiller-Duval bodies?
x: Schiller-Duval bodies mark a yolk sac tumor. Its cells imitate the embryonic yolk sac and secrete alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), which supports the diagnosis and tracks the response to treatment.

w.hCG: hCG comes from trophoblast and marks choriocarcinoma, which shows sheets of trophoblast without villi, not glomerulus-like bodies.
w.LDH: LDH is the marker of dysgerminoma, the clear-cell germ cell tumor that mirrors seminoma of the testis.
w.Inhibin: Inhibin comes from granulosa cells and follows granulosa cell tumors, which show Call-Exner bodies instead.
w.CA-125: CA-125 follows epithelial cancers such as high-grade serous carcinoma, and many benign pelvic conditions also raise it.

pt.say: In the germ cell column, the yolk sac tumor box pairs Schiller-Duval bodies with AFP.

q: Which ovarian tumor shows Call-Exner bodies and coffee-bean nuclei?
x: The granulosa cell tumor forms small follicle-like Call-Exner bodies lined by cells with grooved coffee-bean nuclei. It makes estrogen and inhibin, which cause bleeding and endometrial hyperplasia.

w.Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors form tubules and nests of Leydig cells and make androgens that virilize.
w.Brenner tumor: Brenner tumors also show coffee-bean nuclei, but in nests of transitional-type epithelium without Call-Exner bodies, and they are usually benign.
w.Dysgerminoma: Dysgerminomas grow as sheets of clear fried-egg cells with lymphocyte-rich septa and raise LDH.
w.Thecoma: Thecomas are made of plump, lipid-filled spindle cells that make estrogen but form no follicle-like bodies.

pt.say: The granulosa cell tumor box sits in the sex cord-stromal column, where estrogen and inhibin are its products.

q: Which ovarian tumor causes Meigs syndrome with ascites and a right pleural effusion?
x: An ovarian fibroma is a benign tumor of collagen-making fibroblasts. It can leak fluid that causes ascites and a right pleural effusion, and both clear once the fibroma is removed, which separates Meigs syndrome from cancer.

w.Granulosa cell tumor: Granulosa cell tumors make estrogen and inhibin. Their clues are bleeding and Call-Exner bodies, not effusions that clear after surgery.
w.Mature cystic teratoma: Mature cystic teratomas contain hair, teeth and sebum and are known for torsion, not for ascites with a pleural effusion.
w.Mucinous cystadenoma: Mucinous cystadenomas grow very large and have many chambers. Pseudomyxoma peritonei usually comes from the appendix, not from Meigs syndrome.
w.Dysgerminoma: Dysgerminoma is a malignant germ cell tumor of young women with raised LDH. It does not cause this benign effusion syndrome.

pt.say: The fibroma box in the sex cord-stromal column is labeled Meigs syndrome.

q: Which serum marker is most characteristic of dysgerminoma?
x: Dysgerminoma is the ovarian counterpart of seminoma. It grows as sheets of clear fried-egg cells and typically raises lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). It is very radiosensitive.

w.Alpha-fetoprotein: AFP marks yolk sac tumors. A pure dysgerminoma does not make it, so a high AFP points to another germ cell component.
w.CA-125: CA-125 follows epithelial ovarian cancers, and many benign pelvic conditions also raise it. It does not follow germ cell tumors.
w.Inhibin: Inhibin comes from granulosa cells and follows granulosa cell tumors, which are sex cord-stromal tumors.
w.Carcinoembryonic antigen: Carcinoembryonic antigen rises with mucinous and gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas, including their spread to the ovary, not with dysgerminoma.

pt.say: The dysgerminoma box pairs fried-egg cells with LDH, its lactate dehydrogenase marker.

q: Which ovarian tumor causes hirsutism, a deepening voice and clitoromegaly?
x: The Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, a sex cord-stromal tumor of young women, makes androgens. It causes hirsutism, a deeper voice, clitoromegaly and loss of menses.

w.Granulosa cell tumor: Granulosa cell tumors make estrogen. They cause precocious puberty in girls and bleeding with endometrial hyperplasia in older women.
w.Fibroma: Fibromas make no hormone. They present as a solid mass, sometimes with ascites and a pleural effusion.
w.Brenner tumor: Brenner tumors are usually benign epithelial tumors of transitional-type cells found by chance. They rarely make hormones.
w.Serous cystadenoma: Serous cystadenomas are benign epithelial cysts lined by tubal-type cells. They make no hormone.

pt.say: The Sertoli-Leydig box reads androgens and virilization, which explains her hirsutism and deep voice.

q: Where do most high-grade serous carcinomas begin?
x: Most high-grade serous carcinomas start as serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma in the fimbriated end of the fallopian tube, with an early TP53 mutation. This is why removing the tubes lowers ovarian cancer risk.

w.Ovarian surface epithelium: The ovarian surface was long blamed, but studies of tubes removed from BRCA carriers showed that most of these cancers start in the tube.
w.Endometriotic cysts: Endometriotic cysts give rise to clear cell and endometrioid carcinomas, which follow the slower type I path.
w.Ovarian stroma: Ovarian stroma gives rise to sex cord-stromal tumors such as fibroma, thecoma and granulosa cell tumor.
w.Peritoneal mesothelium: Primary peritoneal carcinoma exists, but most serous carcinoma on the peritoneum has spread there from a tubal primary.

pt.say: The high-grade serous box reads tubal origin, meaning the fimbriated fallopian tube, with TP53 and BRCA.

q: Which gene is mutated in nearly all high-grade serous ovarian carcinomas?
x: TP53 is mutated early in nearly all high-grade serous carcinomas, already in the tubal precursor. This explains their unstable genomes and aggressive course. Germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 variants add to the risk in hereditary cases.

w.KRAS: KRAS mutations drive mucinous tumors and low-grade serous carcinomas, which grow slowly from borderline tumors.
w.BRAF: BRAF mutations mark serous borderline tumors and low-grade serous carcinoma, the type I path.
w.BRCA1: BRCA1 mutations raise the risk of high-grade serous carcinoma, but they are found in only a minority of cases, mostly hereditary ones. TP53 is mutated in nearly all.
w.APC: APC mutations start the adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence in colorectal cancer. They are not a feature of ovarian serous carcinoma.

pt.say: The high-grade serous box lists TP53 alongside its tubal origin and the BRCA link.

q: Which ovarian cysts form when hCG is very high, as in a molar pregnancy?
x: Very high hCG stimulates the LH receptors on theca cells, so both ovaries fill with many-chambered theca lutein cysts. They shrink once the mole is removed or the multiple pregnancy ends.

w.Follicular cysts: Follicular cysts form when one follicle fails to rupture. They are simple and one-sided, and hCG does not cause them.
w.Corpus luteum cysts: A corpus luteum cyst is a single cyst after ovulation that may bleed. Very high hCG does not drive it.
w.Endometriomas: Endometriomas are chocolate cysts of old blood from endometriosis, and they cause cyclic pain and infertility.
w.Paratubal cysts: Paratubal cysts are embryonic remnants in the broad ligament beside the tube. They have nothing to do with hCG.

q: Which vessels are compressed first when an ovary twists on its pedicle?
x: Veins and lymphatics have thin walls and low pressure, so a twist collapses them first while arterial blood still flows in. The ovary swells with edema, and early Doppler can still show arterial flow.

w.Ovarian artery: The ovarian artery is blocked late, after venous congestion raises tissue pressure. That step causes hemorrhagic infarction.
w.Uterine artery: The uterine artery supplies the uterus and joins the ovarian artery, but it is not the vessel twisted in the infundibulopelvic ligament.
w.Internal iliac artery: The internal iliac artery lies on the pelvic sidewall, far from the twisting ovarian pedicle.
w.Inferior epigastric artery: The inferior epigastric artery runs in the front wall of the abdomen and has no part in the ovarian pedicle.

q: Which protective factor removes the tissue where most serous ovarian cancers start?
x: Salpingectomy removes the fimbriated fallopian tube, where serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma begins. This lesion is the precursor of most high-grade serous carcinomas.

w.Breastfeeding: Breastfeeding lowers risk by suppressing ovulation, but it leaves the tube and its epithelium in place.
w.Oral contraceptive use: Oral contraceptives lower ovarian cancer risk by suppressing ovulation, but the tubal precursor cells remain.
w.Multiparity: Each pregnancy lowers risk by pausing ovulation for months, but no tissue is removed.
w.Hysterectomy leaving tubes and ovaries: Removing only the uterus protects little when the fimbriated tubes, where the cancer starts, stay behind.

q: Which bilateral ovarian tumor of signet-ring cells usually comes from the stomach?
x: A Krukenberg tumor is a metastasis, usually from stomach cancer, that fills both ovaries with mucin-making signet-ring cells. Bilateral masses are the clue that the tumor is a metastasis.

w.Brenner tumor: Brenner tumors are usually benign epithelial tumors with nests of transitional-type cells and coffee-bean nuclei.
w.Mucinous cystadenoma: A primary mucinous cystadenoma is a large, cystic, usually one-sided tumor lined by bland columnar cells, not signet-ring cells.
w.Dysgerminoma: Dysgerminoma is a primary germ cell tumor of clear cells with lymphocyte-rich septa, mostly in young women.
w.Granulosa cell tumor: Granulosa cell tumors are primary estrogen-making tumors with Call-Exner bodies, not metastases.

pt.say: The Krukenberg tumor box heads the metastases column: signet-ring cells, usually from the stomach.

q: Which transvaginal ultrasound feature suggests an adnexal mass is benign?
x: A thin-walled, anechoic cyst without solid tissue or flow is almost always benign, often a functional cyst. In a young woman it needs only a repeat scan if it persists.

w.Papillary projection: Papillary projections are solid tissue growing from the cyst wall, and they raise the risk of borderline or malignant epithelial tumors.
w.Thick septations: Thick or irregular septations suggest a many-chambered tumor and raise the chance of cancer.
w.Solid area with flow: Solid tissue with blood flow inside it is the most worrying feature and puts a mass in a high-risk category.
w.Ascites: Ascites with an adnexal mass suggests spread of carcinoma through the peritoneum, or rarely a fibroma with Meigs syndrome.

pt.say: The reassuring panel shows a simple cyst with a thin, smooth wall and anechoic fluid, the benign pattern.

q: Which feature separates a borderline ovarian tumor from an ovarian carcinoma?
x: Borderline tumors show epithelial stratification, papillae and atypia but no destructive stromal invasion. Most behave well, even with noninvasive peritoneal implants. Carcinoma invades the stroma.

w.Epithelial stratification: Stratification of the lining occurs in both borderline tumors and carcinomas, so it cannot separate them.
w.Nuclear atypia: Atypia is present in borderline tumors and carcinomas alike. Its degree helps grade them but does not define invasion.
w.Papillary architecture: Papillae are common to serous borderline tumors and serous carcinomas and say nothing about invasion.
w.Peritoneal implants: Borderline tumors can seed the peritoneum too, although their implants are usually noninvasive.

pt.say: The borderline box in the epithelial column reads no stromal invasion, the feature that separates it from carcinoma.

q: Which symptoms most suggest advanced ovarian carcinoma?
x: Bloating, early satiety and rising abdominal girth come from ascites and omental caking as high-grade serous carcinoma seeds the peritoneum. The symptoms are vague, so most women present at an advanced stage.

w.Sudden severe unilateral pain: Sudden severe one-sided pain with vomiting suggests ovarian torsion or a ruptured cyst, not carcinoma.
w.Cyclic pelvic pain with menses: Cyclic pain with menses points to endometriosis or an endometrioma, which bleed with each cycle.
w.Fever and cervical motion tenderness: Fever with cervical motion tenderness signals pelvic inflammatory disease or a tubo-ovarian abscess.
w.Hirsutism and voice deepening: Virilization points to an androgen-making tumor such as a Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, not epithelial cancer.
